subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw a simple side view: the Arabian Sea, the Western Ghats and the land behind them. Add clouds, rain and arrows to show where the wind comes from and where most rain falls.
prompt_hi: Ek simple side view banao: Arabian Sea, Western Ghats aur unke peeche ki zameen. Baadal, baarish aur teer banao jo dikhayein hawa kahaan se aati hai aur sabse zyada baarish kahaan girti hai.
answer: Arrows from the sea move towards the hills; clouds rise up the western slope with heavy rain on it; few clouds and little rain on the eastern side behind the hills.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Pinky says, 'Islands are just beaches. Nothing lives there except a few coconut trees.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Pinky kehti hai, 'Dweep toh bas beach hote hain. Wahaan kuch coconut ke pedon ke alaawa kuch nahi rehta.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Many islands, like the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, have thick rainforests, mangroves and coral reefs full of life: birds, turtles, crabs, dugongs, wild pigs and much more.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a friend why both the Andaman Islands and the Western Ghats are special places full of life.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko samjhao ki Andaman dweep aur Western Ghats dono jeevan se bhari khaas jagahein kyon hain.
answer: The Andamans are islands with rainforests, mangroves and coral reefs built by tiny animals, home to many sea and land animals. The Western Ghats are hills along the west coast that get heavy monsoon rain on the sea-facing side, so thick forests grow with rare animals found nowhere else. Both are warm and wet, so life is rich.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: which side of the Western Ghats gets more rain, the side facing the sea or the far side?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Western Ghats ki kaunsi taraf zyada baarish hoti hai, samudra wali ya doosri taraf?
answer: The side facing the sea, the west.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Name three things you would carry or do on a trek so that you leave no trash behind.
prompt_hi: Trek pe 3 cheezein batao jo tum saath le jaoge ya karoge taaki koi kachra peeche na chhoote.
answer: Any three: carry a refillable steel bottle, take a cloth bag for snacks and for bringing wrappers back, avoid packaged food, and put all waste back in your bag to throw in a bin at home or in town.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict first: if each of 5,000 visitors to a waterfall leaves just one plastic bottle in a season, what will the area look like by the end? Then work out how many bottles that is.
prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: agar ek jharne pe aane waale 5,000 log ek season mein bas ek-ek plastic bottle chhod dein, toh season ke aakhir tak wahaan ka haal kaisa hoga? Phir hisaab lagao kitni bottlein hui.
answer: 5,000 bottles. Heaps of plastic would choke the stream, spoil its beauty and harm fish and animals; small acts add up.

subject: evs
prompt_en: At a hill station, tourists feed monkeys chips every day. Predict how the monkeys will behave after a few months.
prompt_hi: Ek hill station pe tourist roz bandaron ko chips khilaate hain. Guess karo kuch mahino baad bandar kaisa bartaav karenge.
answer: They stop looking for their natural food and depend on people; they snatch bags and food, may bite, and can fall sick from salty, fried food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict: if everyone takes a shortcut across a grassy hill slope instead of using the path, what will the slope look like after one monsoon?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar sab log raaste ki jagah ghaas wali pahadi dhalaan se shortcut lein, toh ek monsoon ke baad dhalaan kaisi dikhegi?
answer: The grass gets trampled and dies, leaving bare soil; the rain then washes the soil away, cutting gullies and causing mud slides.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do forest guards ask visitors to stay on the marked path and keep quiet?
prompt_hi: Jungle ke guard tourists ko nishaan wale raaste pe rehne aur shaant rehne ko kyon kehte hain?
answer: Paths protect plants and soil from trampling; noise scares animals and disturbs their feeding and nesting; staying on paths also keeps visitors safe.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare two tourist groups at a beach in Lakshadweep. Group A collects shells and pieces of coral as souvenirs and leaves wrappers behind. Group B takes only photos and carries its waste back. What does each leave for the next visitors?
prompt_hi: Lakshadweep ke beach pe do tourist groups ki tulna karo. Group A yaadgaar ke liye seepiyaan aur coral ke tukde le jaata hai aur wrapper chhod deta hai. Group B sirf photo leta hai aur apna kachra wapas le jaata hai. Har group agle logon ke liye kya chhodta hai?
answer: Group A leaves fewer shells and less coral, so hermit crabs and fish lose homes, plus litter; taking coral is also against the law in India. Group B leaves the beach clean and alive for everyone who comes next.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your school is going on a picnic to a park with a lake. Make three rules for your class so the park stays as nice as it was.
prompt_hi: Tumhara school ek jheel wale park mein picnic pe ja raha hai. Apni class ke liye 3 niyam banao taaki park waisa hi achha rahe jaisa tha.
answer: Any three: no littering and carry waste back, do not feed the ducks or fish junk food, do not pluck flowers, stay on the paths, no loud music, keep the lake water clean.

subject: evs
prompt_en: An old fort near your town has names scratched on its walls. Why is this harmful, and what could your class do about it?
prompt_hi: Tumhare shehar ke paas ek purane kile ki deewaron pe naam khurche hue hain. Ye nuksaandeh kyon hai, aur tumhari class iske liye kya kar sakti hai?
answer: Scratching damages a monument that can never be replaced and spoils history for everyone. The class could make posters, talk to visitors, report damage to the caretakers or the Archaeological Survey of India, and never scratch walls themselves.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Make a 'Visitor Code' poster for the Western Ghats with four pictures and one short line each.
prompt_hi: Western Ghats ke liye ek 'Visitor Code' poster banao jismein chaar tasveerein hon aur har ek ke saath ek chhoti line.
answer: Four clear rules, for example: carry back your waste; never feed animals; stay on the trail; use a refillable bottle; keep music off; respect local rules.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bunty says, 'We are only tourists. We come for two days and go. How can we harm the place?' What would you tell him?
prompt_hi: Bunty kehta hai, 'Hum toh bas tourist hain. Do din ke liye aate hain aur chale jaate hain. Hum jagah ko kaise nuksaan pahuncha sakte hain?' Tum use kya bologe?
answer: Each visitor's waste, noise and damage add up with thousands of others; even a short visit can leave litter, scare animals, and break coral and plants.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Before your family's trip to the hills, explain to your cousin how tourists can harm a place and three things your family will do to protect it.
prompt_hi: Family ke pahadon wale trip se pehle apne cousin ko samjhao ki tourist kisi jagah ko kaise nuksaan pahunchaate hain, aur tumhari family use bachaane ke liye 3 kya kaam karegi.
answer: Harm comes from litter, noise, feeding animals, plucking plants and leaving paths, and many small acts add up. Family actions: carry waste back, use steel bottles and cloth bags, stay on paths, keep quiet near animals, never feed wildlife, follow local rules.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: why is 'just one wrapper' a problem in a popular place?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kisi mashhoor jagah pe 'bas ek wrapper' kyon pareshaani hai?
answer: Because thousands of visitors each leave 'just one', and together it becomes a huge pile of waste.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What gives energy to each of these: a flying kite, a spinning ceiling fan, you running a race, a moving car?
prompt_hi: In sabko energy kahaan se milti hai: udti patang, ghoomta pankha, race mein daudte hue tum, aur chalti car?
answer: Kite: the wind. Fan: electricity. You: food. Car: fuel such as petrol, diesel or CNG, or electricity for an electric car.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Make a paper pinwheel (firki) by folding paper; ask an adult if anything needs cutting. Hold it still in a room with no breeze, then in a breeze outside, then blow on it hard. Predict: when will it spin fastest?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz ko mod ke ek firki banao; kuch kaatna ho toh kisi bade se kehna. Pehle use bina hawa wale kamre mein pakdo, phir bahar hawa mein, phir zor se phoonk maaro. Guess karo: kab sabse tez ghoomegi?
answer: It does not spin in still air; it spins in the breeze and fastest when you blow hard, because stronger moving air has more energy to push it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put a dark cloth and a white cloth side by side in the sun for 30 minutes. Predict: which one will feel warmer when you touch it?
prompt_hi: Ek gehre rang ka kapda aur ek safed kapda saath-saath 30 minute dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo: chhoone pe kaunsa zyada garam lagega?
answer: The dark cloth. It takes in more of the Sun's energy, which turns into heat; the white cloth reflects more of the sunlight.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Stand some empty plastic bottles in a row. Roll a ball gently at them, then roll it hard. Predict: which roll will knock down more bottles, and why?
prompt_hi: Kuch khaali plastic bottlein line mein khadi karo. Ek baar ball dheere se lurhkao, phir zor se. Guess karo: kis baar zyada bottlein girengi, aur kyon?
answer: The hard roll. A faster-moving ball has more energy, so it can push more bottles over. We do not see the energy itself; we see what it does.

subject: evs
prompt_en: We say the energy in your food came from the Sun. Explain how.
prompt_hi: Hum kehte hain ki tumhare khaane ki energy Suraj se aayi. Samjhao kaise.
answer: Plants use sunlight to make their own food and store it in their leaves, grains and fruits. We eat plants, or animals that ate plants, so the energy in our food started as sunlight.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do you feel tired and hungry after playing football for an hour?
prompt_hi: Ek ghanta football khelne ke baad tum thake hue aur bhookhe kyon mehsoos karte ho?
answer: Your body used a lot of the energy it got from food to run and kick; it needs more food to get energy again.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a pair of bullocks pulling a plough with a tractor pulling a plough. Where does each get its energy from?
prompt_hi: Hal kheenchte bailon ki jodi aur hal kheenchte tractor ki tulna karo. Dono ko energy kahaan se milti hai?
answer: The bullocks get energy from the grass and fodder they eat, which got its energy from the Sun. The tractor gets energy from diesel burnt in its engine. Both need energy to do the work.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Trace where the energy for the fan in your room comes from, going back as many steps as you can.
prompt_hi: Tumhare kamre ke pankhe ki energy kahaan se aati hai, jitne peeche ke steps tak jaa sako, utna batao.
answer: The fan runs on electricity that comes through wires from a power station. Much of India's electricity is made by burning coal; some comes from falling water at dams, from wind and from sunlight on solar panels. Coal formed long ago from plants, which got their energy from the Sun.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In Tamil Nadu and Gujarat there are rows of tall windmills (wind turbines) near the coast. How do they help a family in a faraway city watch TV?
prompt_hi: Tamil Nadu aur Gujarat mein samudra ke paas lambi-lambi windmills (wind turbines) ki kataarein hain. Ye kisi door shehar ki family ko TV dekhne mein kaise madad karti hain?
answer: The wind turns the blades, which turn a generator that makes electricity; the electricity travels through wires to homes far away, where it runs the TV.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw an energy chain with arrows: Sun, wheat plant, roti, you, cycling to school. Write under each arrow what is happening.
prompt_hi: Teer ke saath ek energy chain banao: Suraj, gehoon ka paudha, roti, tum, school cycle se jaana. Har teer ke neeche likho kya ho raha hai.
answer: Sun to plant: the plant uses sunlight to make food. Plant to roti: wheat grain is ground and cooked into roti. Roti to you: your body takes energy from the food. You to cycling: your muscles push the pedals and the cycle moves.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Tina says, 'In a torch, the electricity goes into the bulb and gets used up there, so it never comes back to the battery.' What's the better idea?
prompt_hi: Tina kehti hai, 'Torch mein bijli bulb mein jaakar wahin khatam ho jaati hai, isliye kabhi battery mein wapas nahi aati.' Behtar samajh kya hai?
answer: The current flows in a complete loop: from the battery, through the bulb and back to the battery. The bulb turns energy from the battery into light and heat. When the battery's stored energy runs low, the torch gets dim.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin what energy is, using three examples from your home.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki energy kya hoti hai, ghar ki 3 misaalon ke saath.
answer: Energy is something we cannot see that makes things move, heat up, light up or make sound. Examples: food gives us energy to play; electricity runs the fan and the bulb; sunlight dries clothes; the LPG flame cooks food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name four sources of energy.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: energy ke chaar srot batao.
answer: Any four: food, the Sun, wind, flowing water, fuels such as petrol, diesel, LPG, coal and wood, electricity, batteries.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Sort these into 'will run out' and 'will not run out': coal, sunlight, petrol, wind, LPG gas, flowing river water.
prompt_hi: Inhe 'khatam ho jayega' aur 'khatam nahi hoga' mein baanto: koyla, dhoop, petrol, hawa, LPG gas, behta nadi ka paani.
answer: Will run out: coal, petrol, LPG. Will not run out: sunlight, wind, flowing river water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: An old ceiling fan uses about 75 watts. If it runs 2 extra hours a day with nobody in the room, predict first: will it waste a tiny bit or a lot in a month? Then work it out: 75 watts for 2 hours is 150 watt-hours a day. How many units is that in 30 days, if 1 unit is 1,000 watt-hours?
prompt_hi: Ek purana ceiling fan lagbhag 75 watt bijli leta hai. Agar woh roz 2 ghante khaali kamre mein faltu chale, toh pehle guess karo: mahine mein thodi si bijli barbaad hogi ya bahut? Phir hisaab lagao: 75 watt 2 ghante = 150 watt-hour roz. 30 din mein kitne unit hue, agar 1 unit = 1,000 watt-hour?
answer: 150 times 30 is 4,500 watt-hours, which is 4.5 units a month for one fan; if 100 homes in a colony do the same, it is 450 units a month, a lot of electricity.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A room's old yellow bulb (60 watts) is replaced with an LED bulb (9 watts) that gives about the same light. Predict: which bulb gets hotter when it is on, and which uses less electricity? (Never touch a lit bulb.)
prompt_hi: Kamre ka purana peela bulb (60 watt) badal ke LED bulb (9 watt) lagaya, jo lagbhag utni hi roshni deta hai. Guess karo: jalte waqt kaunsa bulb zyada garam hota hai, aur kaunsa kam bijli leta hai? (Jalte bulb ko kabhi mat chhoona.)
answer: The old yellow bulb gets much hotter and uses more electricity, because most of its energy turns into heat instead of light; the LED uses only about one-sixth as much for the same light.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict: if every home in India switched off one unneeded light every evening, what would change at coal power stations?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar India ka har ghar roz shaam ek faltu batti band kar de, toh koyle wale bijli ghar mein kya badlega?
answer: They would need to burn less coal, so less coal would be used up and less smoke would go into the air.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why does saving electricity also help keep our air cleaner?
prompt_hi: Bijli bachaane se hamari hawa bhi saaf kyon rehti hai?
answer: Much of India's electricity is made by burning coal in power stations, which gives out smoke and harmful gases; using less electricity means less coal is burnt.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why can a 5-star fridge cost more in the shop but still save a family money?
prompt_hi: 5-star fridge dukaan mein mehenga hota hai, phir bhi family ke paise kaise bacha sakta hai?
answer: More stars mean it uses less electricity for the same cooling; over the years the family pays smaller electricity bills, which can make up for the higher price.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two ways to go to a market 2 km away: by car with one person in it, or by walking or cycling. Compare the fuel used and the effect on the air.
prompt_hi: 2 km door bazaar jaane ke do tareeke: car mein akele, ya paidal ya cycle se. Indhan (fuel) ke kharch aur hawa pe asar ki tulna karo.
answer: The car burns petrol or diesel and adds smoke to the air; walking or cycling uses no fuel and makes no smoke, using the body's food energy instead, and it is good exercise.

subject: evs
prompt_en: At night, your family's TV, set-top box and phone chargers stay switched on at the wall with small lights glowing. What could you do, and why?
prompt_hi: Raat ko tumhare ghar ka TV, set-top box aur phone charger deewar ke switch pe on rehte hain aur chhoti battiyaan jalti hain. Tum kya kar sakte ho, aur kyon?
answer: Switch them off at the wall switch, or ask an adult to. On standby they still use a little electricity all night, and it adds up.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your school roof gets bright sun all day. The principal asks whether to put solar panels there. Give two reasons for it and one thing to check first.
prompt_hi: Tumhare school ki chhat pe din bhar tez dhoop aati hai. Principal poochhti hain ki kya wahaan solar panel lagayein. Do faayde batao aur ek cheez jo pehle check karni chahiye.
answer: Reasons: sunlight is free and will not run out; the school would use less coal-made electricity, pay smaller bills and cause less smoke. Check: shade from trees or buildings, the cost, how the panels will be kept free of dust, and whether the roof is strong enough.

subject: evs
prompt_en: For one week, each evening count how many lights and fans are left on in empty rooms at home. Draw a bar graph for the 7 days and tell me what it shows.
prompt_hi: Ek hafte tak roz shaam gino ki ghar ke khaali kamron mein kitni battiyaan aur pankhe on reh gaye. 7 din ka bar graph banao aur batao woh kya dikhata hai.
answer: One bar per day showing the count; it shows on which days energy was wasted and whether the family got better; shorter bars over the week mean less waste.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says, 'Our family pays the electricity bill, so leaving the fan on doesn't hurt anyone.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai, 'Bijli ka bill toh hamari family bharti hai, isliye pankha chala chhodne se kisi ka nuksaan nahi hota.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Wasted electricity still has to be made, often by burning coal that pollutes the air everyone breathes and that will run out; small wastes from many homes add up.
